nodes.label: The Capability Architecture, Volume I: Foundations
nodes.author: Sean Burman

nodes.label: Capability Architecture
nodes.rationale: Defines a computational framework for organizations that observe their own operation, revise models of work, and develop governed software capabilities in response, treating capability rather than application as the fundamental unit.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.rationale: A persistent organizational ability that reduces resources, uncertainty, coordination, or expertise required to achieve a class of outcomes; distinct from automation of a known procedure.

nodes.label: Capability Definition
nodes.rationale: Versioned specification of knowledge, authority, inputs, constraints, tools, procedures, tests, and outcome measures required to realize a capability.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.rationale: Identifiable decision-making runtime that pursues goals using knowledge and tools within explicitly defined authority and capability boundaries; a language model alone is not an agent.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.rationale: Recorded occurrence asserting change, action, decision, or observation; distinct from observation as assertion about reality.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.rationale: Timestamped measurement or assertion about organizational reality with source, context, and provenance.

nodes.label: Authority
nodes.rationale: Legitimate and machine-enforceable scope for access, decisions, resource commitment, or state change.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Governed mechanism preserving observations, decisions, models, and outcomes; divided into episodic, semantic, procedural, working, and institutional archive.

nodes.label: Workflow
nodes.rationale: Constrained graph of permitted state transitions; normative structure distinct from empirical process history.

nodes.label: P-001 Theory precedes implementation
nodes.rationale: Implementation may validate or falsify theory, but implementation convenience must not silently define the theory.

nodes.label: P-002 Capability is the product
nodes.rationale: Data, dashboards, and recommendations are intermediate forms; the durable product is improved organizational ability.

nodes.label: P-003 Evolve from observation rather than specification alone
nodes.rationale: Operational system must learn from actual work, friction, exceptions, and outcomes while specifications remain useful.

nodes.label: P-004 Preserve provenance and time
nodes.rationale: Important facts must remain connected to source, observation time, validity interval, and confidence or dispute status.

nodes.label: P-005 Authority explicit and machine-enforceable
nodes.rationale: Every consequential action by human or software agent must be evaluated against a declared source and scope of authority.

nodes.label: P-006 Agents receive bounded autonomy
nodes.rationale: Agents must operate under explicit mandate, authority scope, tool boundary, and evaluation regime.

nodes.label: P-007 Capabilities require outcomes and retirement path
nodes.rationale: Every deployed capability must have an accountable owner, measurable outcomes, review cadence, and retirement conditions.

nodes.label: P-008 Organizational model is plural
nodes.rationale: Event, graph, document, transactional, and analytical representations should coexist as governed projections of shared evidence.

nodes.label: P-009 Human purpose remains external to optimization
nodes.rationale: System may optimize methods and resources but must not silently redefine organizational purpose from behavioral data.

nodes.label: P-010 Uncertainty must remain visible
nodes.rationale: Intelligent systems must represent confidence, missing context, disagreement, and model limits; hidden uncertainty becomes false authority.

nodes.label: H-001 Organizations as temporal knowledge graphs
nodes.rationale: Under investigation: organizations can be usefully represented as dynamic, temporal knowledge graphs.

nodes.label: H-002 Capability as stronger reusable unit
nodes.rationale: Tentatively supported: capability is a stronger unit of reusable organizational intelligence than application feature or workflow.

nodes.label: H-003 Agents are runtime realizations of capabilities
nodes.rationale: Speculative: agents are runtime realizations of capability definitions.

nodes.label: H-004 Observation reveals unarticulated requirements
nodes.rationale: Under investigation: structured observation can reveal software requirements users cannot articulate directly.

nodes.label: H-005 Friction appears as repeated exception handling
nodes.rationale: Under investigation: most persistent operational friction appears first as repeated exception handling.

nodes.label: H-006 Agent value in encoded organizational judgment
nodes.rationale: Speculative: economic value of an agent is primarily encoded organizational judgment, not model access.

nodes.label: H-007 Capability registry supports licensing and transfer
nodes.rationale: Speculative: a capability registry can support composition, licensing, and cross-industry adaptation.

nodes.label: H-008 Outcome-linked event histories reduce learning cost
nodes.rationale: Under investigation: outcome-linked event histories can reduce the cost of organizational learning.

nodes.label: Canonical Event Layer
nodes.rationale: Durable immutable record of occurrences and observations; corrections via superseding events; enables rebuildable projections.

nodes.label: Work-Object Registry
nodes.rationale: Assigns durable identities with consistent type, lifecycle, relationship, and provenance semantics across modules.

nodes.label: Capability Registry
nodes.rationale: Stores versioned capability definitions, dependencies, owners, tests, evaluations, limitations, and deployment status; bridge from discovery to operational change.

nodes.label: Agent Runtime
nodes.rationale: Layered runtime composing identity, mandate, authority, memory, policies, planner, tools, evaluator, and audit stream.

nodes.label: Temporal Attributed Multigraph
nodes.rationale: Baseline formal model G_t = (V_t, E_t, A_t, P_t) with temporal validity for organizational entities and relationships.

nodes.label: Observation-Driven Capability Loop
nodes.rationale: System develops capability by closing a loop between work, observation, modeling, change, and evaluation.

nodes.label: Data to Capability Progression
nodes.rationale: Conceptual progression data → information → insight → decision → capability; intermediates valuable only when they improve ability to act.

nodes.label: Augmentation Rather Than Substitution
nodes.rationale: Architecture removes avoidable cognitive load while preserving meaningful judgment, following Engelbart and Licklider traditions.

nodes.label: IP-001 Plan broadly, commit narrowly
nodes.rationale: Model-assisted components may prepare proposals with rich context; consequential state changes pass through narrow deterministic commands enforcing policy.

nodes.label: Cross-Cutting Governance
nodes.rationale: Identity, access, consent, policy, change approval, audit, and model evaluation make intelligence usable; not a layer below intelligence.

nodes.label: Inference and Discovery Layer
nodes.rationale: Searches for recurring patterns, variants, bottlenecks, and contradictions; results are inspectable hypotheses, not automatic truth.

nodes.label: Control Plane and Operational Plane
nodes.rationale: Operational plane processes day-to-day work; control plane defines schemas, policies, capabilities, versions, and rollout without modifying production data directly.

nodes.label: Model Gateway
nodes.rationale: Centralizes provider access, redaction, versioning, rate limits, and evaluation metadata; enables provider substitution.

nodes.label: Reference Implementation Stack
nodes.rationale: Conservative first stack: Go, React, PostgreSQL, object storage, graph projection, containers, model gateway, OpenTelemetry; theory remains independent of tools.

nodes.label: Evolutionary Deployment Stages
nodes.rationale: Staged adoption from identity and events through process understanding, deterministic capabilities, assisted discovery, bounded agents, then capability generation.

nodes.label: Capability Value Model
nodes.rationale: V(C) approximates outcome-adjusted resource gains minus build, operate, and govern costs; requires explicit baselines and lifecycle costs.

nodes.label: Organizational Routines
nodes.rationale: Carriers of organizational knowledge that can be selected, replicated, and modified; candidates for capability definitions when linked to outcomes.

nodes.label: Cybernetic Feedback
nodes.rationale: Architecture adopts feedback but broadens regulation to revising goals, constraints, roles, and capabilities as organizations learn.

nodes.label: Hayek The Use of Knowledge in Society
nodes.author: F. A. Hayek

nodes.label: Nelson and Winter Evolutionary Theory of Economic Change
nodes.author: R. R. Nelson and S. G. Winter

nodes.label: Organization as Distributed Decision System
nodes.rationale: Organizations coordinate because no participant has complete information; architecture of decision rights, information flow, and coordination cost.

nodes.label: Composite Capability
nodes.rationale: Depends on subordinate capabilities via explicit contracts for guarantees, evidence, and failure modes; reuse through small sub-capabilities and policy layers.
